subparts.derivation: A=[[2,4],[1,2]], det A=4-4=0. Moreover g=2b, so all vertices lie on one line.
subparts.checks: The zero area agrees with linearly dependent columns.
Positive first minor and determinant also show Σ≻0.

subparts.derivation: Swap diagonal entries, negate off-diagonal entries, and divide by determinant.

The inverse transformation is x=A⁻¹y. The derivative ∂x/∂y=A⁻¹ has absolute determinant 1/|ad-bc|. Substitute x into the original exponent: xᵀx=yᵀA⁻ᵀA⁻¹y. Probability conservation fY(y)dy=fX(A⁻¹y)dx supplies the determinant factor.
subparts.checks: |AAᵀ|=(det A)² and (AAᵀ)⁻¹=A⁻ᵀA⁻¹. Substitution y=Ax makes its integral equal the original normalized integral 1, including orientation reversing det A<0.

subparts.derivation: x1=y1/3,x2=y2/2 and |det ∂x/∂y|=1/6. The squared norm becomes y1²/9+y2²/4.
subparts.checks: Covariance diag(9,4) has determinant 36; normalizer is 1/(2π√36). Two one-dimensional Gaussian integrals yield total mass 1.

subparts.derivation: From y2=2x2 get x2=y2/2. From y1=x1+x2 get x1=y1-y2/2.

subparts.checks: This equals 1/det A, with det A=2.

subparts.derivation: Substitute the inverse coordinates into x1²+x2²=(y1-y2/2)²+(y2/2)²=y1²-y1y2+y2²/2 and multiply density by 1/2.
subparts.checks: Σ=AAᵀ=[[2,2],[2,4]], det Σ=4, Σ⁻¹=[[1,-1/2],[-1/2,1/2]]. Its normalizer matches; invertible change of variables proves total integral 1.

subparts.derivation: Let δx=x-μx. Since μy=Aμx+b, δy=Aδx+w. Then Cov(x,y)=E[δx(Aδx+w)ᵀ]=ΣxAᵀ+E[δxwᵀ]. Independence and zero means make the last term zero. Transposing yields Cov(y,x)=AΣx.
subparts.checks: Shapes D×E and E×D, respectively; they are transposes, not generally equal. Diagonality of Q is unnecessary for this result.

subparts.derivation: Mean y is Aμx+b. Center y to Aδx+w; expansion and independent zero-mean noise give Cov(y)=AΣxAᵀ+Q. Stack x and y, placing the supplied cross-covariances into opposite off-diagonal blocks.
subparts.checks: Mean length D+E, covariance (D+E)×(D+E), symmetric. It equals T diag(Σx,Q)Tᵀ with T=[[I,0],[A,I]], so it is positive semidefinite.

subparts.derivation: Let H=(y1,…,yt). Under independent fresh noises, m=Aμt and V=AΣtAᵀ+Q. Next y=Cxt+1+vt+1 has mean Cm, variance CVCᵀ+R and cross covariance Cov(xt+1,yt+1|H)=VCᵀ. Stack these blocks; Gaussianity is supplied.
subparts.conclusion: Under the stated fresh-noise interpretation: N((m;Cm), [[V,VCᵀ],[CV,CVCᵀ+R]]), m=Aμt, V=AΣtAᵀ+Q.
subparts.checks: If state dimension d and observation dimension e, A:d×d,C:e×d,Q,V:d×d,R:e×e. The joint block is positive semidefinite by the same triangular transformation construction. μ0,Σ0 are not needed once μt,Σt are supplied.
assumptions: wt and vt+1 are independent of the current state and observation history, and of each other.
unresolved: The phrase i.i.d. Gaussian noises does not explicitly state independence from x0/the state/history. If it means only independence among noise draws, the usual prediction blocks additionally require exogeneity. Also w and v cannot literally be identically distributed across different dimensions or unequal Q,R; the conventional reading is each process independent over time and mutually independent.
